# Rotary spiral

Type id `rotary_spiral` · category: Rotary · runs in Setups of kind: rotary

One continuous spiral: the part turns while the tool advances along the axis, with no lifts. A finishing type for rotary Setups.

- Takes the material it cuts out of the stock for the toolpaths after it: no.

See [Add a toolpath](Add-a-Toolpath) for how to add one, and the [list of toolpath types](Toolpath-Types).

In the project file a setting is written as `group.key`, for example `passes.stepover`. In the app the inspector shows each group on its own tab. Lengths are in millimetres in the file whatever unit the project shows.

## Tool

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spindle speed | `tool_params.spindle_rpm` | rev/min | from the tool's cutting data (`rpm`) | How fast the spindle turns. Left empty, it comes from the tool's cutting data for the Setup's material. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: tool, Setup material. |
| Feed | `tool_params.feed` | group of settings (below) |  |  |
| Cut feed | `tool_params.feed.cut` | mm/min | from the tool's cutting data (`feed`) | How fast the tool moves while it cuts. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: tool, Setup material. |
| Plunge feed | `tool_params.feed.plunge` | mm/min | from the tool's cutting data (`plunge`) | How fast the tool moves straight down into the material. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: tool, Setup material. |
| Ramp | `tool_params.feed.ramp` | mm/min | calculated from feed.cut | Feed while the tool ramps into the material. Left empty, it is the cut feed. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `feed.cut`. |
| Lead in | `tool_params.feed.lead_in` | mm/min | calculated from feed.cut | Feed on the lead-in move. Left empty, it is the cut feed. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `feed.cut`. |
| Lead out | `tool_params.feed.lead_out` | mm/min | calculated from feed.lead_in | Feed on the lead-out move. Left empty, it is the lead-in feed. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `feed.lead_in`. |
| Transition | `tool_params.feed.transition` | mm/min | calculated from feed.cut | Feed on the short moves that link one pass to the next while the tool stays down. Left empty, it is the cut feed. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `feed.cut`. |
| Coolant | `tool_params.coolant` | `off`, `flood`, `mist` | `off` | Coolant to switch on for this toolpath. The post must have a coolant block, or you get a warning. Depends on: post `coolant_on` event. |

## Geometry

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Drive faces | `geometry.drive_faces` | selection of bodies, faces or edges | calculated from all faces of the Setup's bodies | The faces this toolpath machines. 3-D types machine every face of the Setup's bodies when this is empty; 2-D types need something selected. Allowed: faces of the Setup's bodies. Depends on: Setup `geometry`. |
| Check faces | `geometry.check_faces` | selection of bodies, faces or edges | calculated from faces not in drive_faces or excluded_faces | Faces the tool must not cut into. Left empty, every face that is not a drive face or an excluded face. Depends on: `drive_faces`, `excluded_faces`. |
| Excluded faces | `geometry.excluded_faces` | selection of bodies, faces or edges | not set | Faces to leave out: the tool is allowed to cut into them. |
| X start | `geometry.x_start` | position along X: `ref` and `offset` in mm | `model_left` | Where along the rotary axis the toolpath starts. |
| X end | `geometry.x_end` | position along X: `ref` and `offset` in mm | `model_right` | Where along the rotary axis the toolpath ends. It must be beyond the start. |

## Heights

A height is a reference plus an offset in mm, for example `{ ref = "stock_top", offset = 5 }`. The reference is one of `setup_clearance`, `stock_top`, `stock_bottom`, `model_top`, `model_bottom`, `work_zero`, `selection`.

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clearance | `heights.clearance` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `setup_clearance` | The height the tool rises to for the longest moves, above everything including clamps. Allowed: ≥ `retract`. Depends on: Setup clearance. |
| Retract | `heights.retract` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `stock_top` + 5 | The height the tool rises to between cuts. It must not be below the feed height. Allowed: ≥ `feed`. Depends on: stock. |
| Feed | `heights.feed` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `top` + 2 | The height where the tool changes from rapid to cutting feed on its way down. It is measured from the top height. Allowed: ≥ `top`. Depends on: `top`. |
| Top | `heights.top` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `model_top` | The top of the material this toolpath cuts. The first cut starts here. Allowed: > `bottom` (≥ for `parallel`). Depends on: per type. |
| Bottom | `heights.bottom` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `model_bottom` | The bottom of the cut: the lowest point the tool reaches. Depends on: per type. |

## Passes

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Machining tolerance | `passes.machining_tolerance` | mm | 0.01 | How far the calculated path may stray from the ideal path. A smaller number gives a smoother path and a longer program. Allowed: ≥ 1e-4. |
| Max segment length | `passes.max_segment_length` | mm | not set | Longest straight move in the path. Left empty, there is no limit. Allowed: > 0. |
| Output arcs | `passes.output_arcs` | yes or no | yes | Write arcs as arc moves (G2 and G3) where the path has them. Off writes only straight moves. Depends on: post arc support. |
| Advance | `passes.advance` | mm | from the tool's cutting data (`stepover`) | How far the tool moves along the axis for each turn of the spiral. Allowed: (0, D]. Depends on: tool, material; not with `scallop_height`. |
| Scallop height | `passes.scallop_height` | mm | not set | Choose the stepover so the ridges between passes are no higher than this. It needs a tool with a rounded tip. Set this or a stepover, not both. Allowed: (0, r). Depends on: tool shape. |
| Direction | `passes.direction` | `climb`, `conventional` | `climb` | Which way the tool travels. `climb` has the material on the right of the tool as it moves (with a clockwise spindle), `conventional` the opposite. `zigzag` alternates direction on every pass, and `any`, `selection` and `reversed` follow the curves as selected. |
| Start | `passes.start` | `x_start`, `x_end` | `x_start` | Whether the spiral starts at the start or the end of the range. |
| Stock to leave | `passes.stock_to_leave` | mm | 0 | Material left on the walls for a later finishing pass. A negative value cuts past the model, which is useful for inlays. Allowed: 2-D types: > −R; 3-D types: > −r (corner radius; ≥ 0 for flat tools) (§7, decision 3). Depends on: tool. |

## Linking

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retract | `linking.retract` | `full`, `minimum`, `stay_down` | `minimum` | How the tool moves between passes: `full` always lifts to the retract height, `minimum` lifts only as far as needed, `stay_down` keeps the tool in the material when the straight move is clear. |
| Safety distance | `linking.safety_distance` | mm | 1 | How far above the highest point on the way the tool lifts when it retracts the minimum amount. Allowed: ≥ 0. Depends on: `retract` = `minimum`. |
| Transitions | `linking.transitions` | `direct`, `smooth` | `direct` | Whether the short moves between passes go straight or are smoothed. Depends on: `retract` ≠ `full`. |
| Lead in | `linking.lead_in` | group of settings (below) |  |  |
| Kind | `linking.lead_in.kind` | `none`, `arc`, `linear` | `none` | How the tool eases into the cut: not at all, along a quarter circle, or along a straight line. |
| Radius | `linking.lead_in.radius` | mm | calculated from 0.5 * tool.diameter | Radius of an arc lead-in. Left empty, half the tool diameter. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `lead_in.kind` = `arc`. |
| Length | `linking.lead_in.length` | mm | calculated from 0 (arc) or tool.radius (linear) | Length of the straight part of the lead-in. Allowed: ≥ 0. Depends on: `lead_in.kind`. |
| Lead out | `linking.lead_out` | group of settings (below) |  | Depends on: `lead_in`. |
| Kind | `linking.lead_out.kind` | `none`, `arc`, `linear` | `none` | How the tool eases out of the cut. Left empty, the same as the lead-in. |
| Radius | `linking.lead_out.radius` | mm | calculated from 0.5 * tool.diameter | Radius of an arc lead-out. |
| Length | `linking.lead_out.length` | mm | calculated from 0 (arc) or tool.radius (linear) | Length of the straight part of the lead-out. |
